verdict: Yes: merge f0fc8b2cd (their commit edd147a7e plus one repair of mine, e37a3fec0, and the review notes and results; nothing else in the engine is touched). On the 240 local dumps simple probing on an equation (R1, milestone M2) reaches exactly what HiGHS reaches with the same rule: HiGHS changes eight instances between its references m1_a and m2_a, the engine the same eight, by the same number of nonzeros, rows and columns on each. The gain of the family is 1.0103 / 1.0106 / 1.0220 (nonzeros / rows / columns, geometric mean over the 237 instances without ex9, ex10, enlight_hard) against HiGHS's own 1.0103 / 1.0105 / 1.0219; the engine stands at 1.0021 / 1.0023 / 1.0023 of m2_a; no instance is larger than before in default or primal-only mode; the cost is +1.8% of the engine's time on the 240 (noise 0.3%). Every size, work, round and flag number of the author that I measured again is right. The four instances below 0.99 of m2_a are those of the growth limit of the singleton family from M1 and did not move. No guard of the rule refuses a single row on the 240 or the 17 local dumps, and each guard loosened alone and all together gives the commit's reduced-model hash on every instance, so none of the assumptions has a measurable worth on these sets. One defect of worth and cost was in the commit and is repaired with a failing test first: a binary that is the binary of many probing rows was charged on the budget once per row, the charge grew with the square of the rows, and with 5,000 such rows the engine ended on max_rounds with 3,467 of them left. The same charge exists in the doubleton equations of the base (Stage 1 code); I repaired it too, on a branch of its own (review-stage1c-m2-worth-2-doubleton, a072b69c54e2c402cc277e06a2acff30e4f18ce0), because it changes Stage 1 statistics: the owner or the merge decides whether to take it. One statement of the author's report is wrong (how HiGHS counts fixed columns of a probing row); it changes no conclusion. Not done: anything with a solver, the node, the 44 testbed instances, solution quality.
wrong_results: No wrong reduction was found by this review. My side was worth and cost; the campaigns of the milestone are the validity reviewer's, and I ran campaigns only for my two repairs.

Broken cost contract of the design, repaired (commit e37a3fec08d4de265e0e98ac809f356991fdb0b3). The design's cost paragraph for simple probing (R1) says the live entries of the substituted columns and of their roots are spent once per call; take() in src/rules_simple_probing.cpp spent the entries of every column of a row that entered the batch, the binary's included, once per row. Failing input: rows 2 p - x[i] - y[i] = 0 over binaries that share p (scratch tools/make_hub.py; now the test columns_probing_shared_binary_is_spent_once). What happened on edd147a7e, release build: 600 rows need 3 calls of the family and 5 rounds; 2,000 rows 14 calls and 16 rounds; 5,000 rows end on max_rounds after 20 calls with 3,467 rows left and no fixed-point flag; 20,000 rows end with 18,825 left. The true work is 20 units per row. Findings are booked when the batch is applied, so the stall limit (100,000 units + 2 passes) ends the collection. After the repair a column is spent when it enters the batch: 5,000, 20,000 and 200,000 rows are reduced to nothing in one call of the family and 3 rounds (0.09 s for 200,000). No condition of the rule is touched, only the amount given to work_budget_t::spend. On the 240 and the 17 local dumps the repair changes nothing but the work of the family on three instances.

The author's test of the work of the chain model (columns_probing_chain_moves_every_entry_once) was an inequality that let the charge per row pass (1,658 units where every column spent once gives 1,600). It is an equality now; it fails on edd147a7e. Repaired in the same commit.
other_defects: Base defect of the same class, not of this milestone, repaired on a separate branch only (review-stage1c-m2-worth-2-doubleton, commit a072b69c54e2c402cc277e06a2acff30e4f18ce0, one commit on top of f0fc8b2cd). The doubleton equations (src/rules_doubleton.cpp:90) spend for an edge the live entries of both its columns, which is what their contract in rules.hpp (d) says. One column in k doubleton equations is charged k times its entries. Model: x[i] - p = 0 for integer columns in [0, 5], every x[i] in one more row (scratch tools/make_hub2.py). Base binary and the reviewed commit alike: 2,000 equations need 12 calls and 14 rounds; 5,000 end on max_rounds with 2,975 of 5,001 rows left and no fixed-point flag; 20,000 end with 18,364 of 20,001 left. On the 240 local dumps the family already stops on its budget in its first call on traininstance2 and traininstance6 (1,175,188 and 942,248 units charged, 185,300 and 145,392 with a column spent once), which costs one call of six families each and no reduction. With the repair: 600 to 200,000 equations reduced to nothing in two calls and three rounds; 497 tests pass in both builds; on the 240 local dumps in default mode, primal-only mode and with simple probing off the reduced-model hash, sizes, rounds and flags equal edd147a7e's on all 240, the work of the doubleton family is lower on 51 instances (110,424,674 to 106,074,973 units in default mode). It is apart because an off run of that engine no longer equals the engine before the milestone in the work and calls of the Stage 1 families, which criterion 2 of the author's task asks for.

The author's report and the message of commit edd147a7e say that HiGHS counts 296,239 substitutions 'of which 5,616 are columns of a probing row that were fixed already'. That is wrong: baseline/highs_diag.patch counts a fixed column before the `continue` and a substitution after it, so the 5,616 are apart from the 296,239. HiGHS makes 2,894 real substitutions on each cryptanalysis instance where the engine makes 272. It changes no conclusion: the net effect of the rule is equal on both sides on every instance (364 columns, 516 rows, 1,580 nonzeros on each cryptanalysis instance; 254,430 columns on highschool1-aigio; 10,720 on brazil3).

The time on bab2 and bab6 beyond the family, which the author left open as possibly noise, is real and traced. In work units, which do not depend on the load: the other families do 23.9% more work on bab2 (27,365,329 to 33,915,401: tightening +3,269,192, parallel rows +2,456,140, propagation +823,276) and 21.9% more on bab6. The 132 and 120 columns of the batch lie in 186 and 178 rows that stay, with 830,023 and 515,124 entries; each of these long rows gets a changed entry and is read again by the cascade and the parallel rows. Cost +12.0 ms (+11%) and +7.1 ms (+10%) for 388 and 440 nonzeros. Inherent to substituting into long rows; there is no limit for it and I built none.

Findings are booked when the batch is applied, never while it is collected, so the budget that ends a collecting call is the stall limit (100,000 units + 2 passes), not the limit of 4 passes. With the repair the work of a collecting call is linear, but a model whose columns are dense and nearly all in probing rows could still stop a call half way and need a round more. Not seen: 0 of 455 calls stop on the 240 local dumps, the largest first call is 0.80 passes (sorrell3).

Cost, small, not repaired: 546,515 visits on the 240 local dumps pass the balance test and are scanned, and 520,744 of them (110 instances; neos-5114902-kasavu 218,568) hold no binary: rows whose two activities are symmetric about the side. They are scanned again each time they are listed. That is 4.2 million slots, 3.6% of the family's work units; 9.5 ms on kasavu (2.7% of its presolve).

Cost of a guard that never fires on real instances: the test of the size of an offset reads every column of every row that a binary splits, once per call: 300,951 column scans and 1,234,491 entries on the 240 local dumps, 1,062,430 of them on highschool1-aigio, where they are 31% of the family's work. It refuses no row on the 240 or the 17.

Assumptions without a switch, as the author says in not_done: the 0/1 bounds of the binary, explicit bounds only, one batch per call, the order of the binaries, the place in the round, and the rounding and size guards that share tol.zero and tol.side_error. I measured each that can be loosened in a scratch build (see assumptions); none is built into the commit, and I added none: a switch that loosens a validity condition is not a worth reviewer's to add.

The design's citations that I used agree with the code: the balance test of HiGHS at HPresolve.cpp:2695-2698 of the pristine 1.16 source, and the cost paragraph of R1. I did not recheck the others; the author's list of moved lines stands as he reports it.

assumptions.title: The binary and every other integer column of range 1 have the bounds 0 and 1
assumptions.statement: Simple probing (R1) takes only an integer column with bounds exactly 0 and 1 as the binary and leaves a row that holds another integer column with bounds one apart that are not 0 and 1. The design takes any integer column with upper - lower == 1.
assumptions.switch: no switch (scratch switch W_UNIT=design in s1c_m2_worth/tools/instrument.py)
assumptions.alternatives: The design's condition; HiGHS's condition (range within the feasibility tolerance of 1).
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps and 17 local dumps, default and primal-only: 0 rows refused; with the design's condition the reduced-model hash is the commit's on all 240 and all 17. In no scanned row of the 240 is there an integer column whose range is within 1e-6 of 1 and not 1. (Author's campaign: 607,630 visits left in 163.2 million random release models.)

assumptions.title: Limit on the scale of an alias
assumptions.statement: Every other column of the row has upper - lower <= 1e6; beyond it the row is left.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 0 rows refused, the largest scale applied is 1 on all eight instances; with 1e300 and with 1 the reduced-model hash is the commit's on all 240. 17 local dumps: 0 refused.

assumptions.title: Tolerance of the balance test
assumptions.statement: A row is scanned only when |(M - b) - (b - m)| less the two error bounds is at most one feasibility tolerance.
assumptions.alternatives: 2, which the two forcing tests allow by themselves; larger.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 524,133 visits fail the balance; 141 of them (all on momentum1) are within 10 tolerances and 206 (3 instances) within 1e4; none of these rows has a binary. With 2, 10 and 1e4 the reduced-model hash is the commit's on all 240.

assumptions.title: Tolerance of the two forcing tests and their rounding-only form
assumptions.statement: Each conditional row is forcing in the engine's sense: the gap within tol.feasibility * min|a| / max(1, max|a|) over the entries other than the binary, and with a continuous column among them positive only by the error bound of the activity plus 8 rounding units of the terms.
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own: tolerances_t::feasibility and the constant forcing_rounding_units = 8 that the forcing row shares (scratch switch W_FORCING=abs)
assumptions.alternatives: The absolute feasibility tolerance alone; HiGHS's absolute 1e-9 on the balance and on the coefficient.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 25,771 rows are tried with a binary, 0 are refused by the forcing test (0 for its tolerance, 0 for the rounding-only form). With the absolute tolerance alone the reduced-model hash is the commit's on all 240. Of the 520,744 scanned rows without a binary, 0 would have one under HiGHS's plain test.

assumptions.title: A continuous column whose range is rounding is left
assumptions.statement: A row is left when a continuous column of it has bound_rounding(lower) + bound_rounding(upper) above tol.zero times its range, or when the positive part of a gap is above tol.zero times the smallest |a| * range among its continuous columns.
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own: tolerances_t::zero = 1e-9
assumptions.alternatives: Another factor; treating such a column as a constant of the row. No test at all is wrong (the author's campaign).
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps and 17 local dumps, both modes: 0 rows refused.

assumptions.title: Size of an offset
assumptions.statement: For the binary and every other column, max(|lower|, |upper|) times the largest coefficient of the column times tol.side_error must not exceed tol.feasibility, and every finite side of a row of the column must be readable; a row left for this alone makes the call report limited.
assumptions.switch: no switch of its own: tolerances_t::side_error = 1e-14 and tolerances_t::feasibility
assumptions.alternatives: No such test, as the doubleton equations have none; a test of each shifted side instead of a size.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps and 17 local dumps: 0 rows refused, 0 calls report limited. Its cost: 300,951 column scans and 1,234,491 entries on the 240, 1,062,430 of them on highschool1-aigio (31% of the family's work there).

assumptions.title: Explicit bounds only
assumptions.statement: The activities are over explicit bounds; a recorded implied bound is never read, and a row with an infinite term in an activity is left. HiGHS reads implied bounds.
assumptions.switch: no switch (scratch switch W_IMPLIED=1: an equation that passes only with the valid recorded implied bounds of its continuous columns from other rows gets them as explicit bounds first)
assumptions.alternatives: Reading the implied bounds of continuous columns (integer columns have none in this engine: propagation writes their bounds explicitly).
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 637,520 visits on 78 instances end at an infinite term. Counted at every call over every live equation with three or more free entries, listed or not (3,018,663 row tests): 1,131,368 have a tighter valid implied bound on a continuous column from another row; with these bounds read, 0 rows pass balance and binary that do not pass on explicit bounds (394,703 listed rows on 18 instances pass the balance, none has a binary). With the scratch switch the reduced-model hash is the commit's on all 240 in both modes and on all 17. neos-1445765: no listed row has such an implied bound; its 18,444 aliases come in the first call and equal HiGHS's count.

assumptions.title: One batch per call; a connected row waits
assumptions.statement: A row is taken into the batch only when no two of its free columns are connected by the batch already; otherwise it goes back on the list for the next call.
assumptions.switch: no switch (scratch switch W_SERVE=1: the call repeats its pass while a row was pushed back)
assumptions.alternatives: Serving the list until it stays empty inside one call.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 952 visits wait, 476 on each cryptanalysis instance; none of them gives an alias later (the batch changes those rows) and both instances end at the reference's sizes. Served in the same call: the same hash and the same rounds on all 240, two passes more.

assumptions.title: Order of the binaries
assumptions.statement: The columns that can be the binary are tried in increasing column index and the first that passes every limit is taken.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 25,771 rows have a candidate and each is taken or pushed back with its first candidate (25,771 tries), so the order decides nothing there.

assumptions.title: Budget of the family, and when a finding is booked
assumptions.statement: 4 passes, 2 stall passes, floor 100,000 work units per call. A finding is booked when the batch is applied, so while a call collects, the stall limit (floor + 2 passes) is the one that stops it.
assumptions.alternatives: Other values; booking a taken row as progress when it enters the batch.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: 0 of 455 calls stop (0 of 425 in primal-only mode), the largest first call is 0.80 passes, all later calls together at most 0.69. 17 local dumps: 0 stops.

assumptions.title: The entries of a column are spent once per call (my repair)
assumptions.statement: A column is charged on the budget when it enters the batch, not once per row of the batch that holds it. Before the repair the charge was per row, against the design's cost paragraph.
assumptions.alternatives: The charge per row of the reviewed commit.
assumptions.measured: Rows 2 p - x - y = 0 that share p, release build: per row, 5,000 rows end on max_rounds with 3,467 left and 20,000 with 18,825 left; once per call, 5,000, 20,000 and 200,000 rows are reduced to nothing in one call. 240 local dumps and 17 local dumps, both modes: the same hash, sizes, rounds and flags either way; the family's work is 3,466,948 against 3,425,072 units on highschool1-aigio and 692,060 against 677,704 on each cryptanalysis instance.

assumptions.title: Place in the round
assumptions.statement: The family runs once per round, after the doubleton equations and before the singleton columns.

assumptions.title: On in primal-only mode
assumptions.statement: The rule runs in primal-only mode: every feasible point satisfies the aliases.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, primal-only: the same 277,320 aliases on the same eight instances; 1.0103 / 1.0105 / 1.0219 against the engine before in that mode, none larger.

assumptions.title: No limit on what an alias costs the other families
assumptions.statement: A row is taken whatever the rows of its columns are; the rows that receive a moved entry are read again by the cascade and the parallel rows.
assumptions.alternatives: A limit on the entries of the rows that receive entries, against the entries the batch removes.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps: bab2 +12.0 ms (+11%) and +23.9% work units of the other families for 388 nonzeros less; bab6 +7.1 ms (+10%) and +21.9% for 440. On the other six instances with a finding the rule removes far more than it costs.

assumptions.title: Root of a tree of the batch
assumptions.statement: The shared alias forest picks as root an integer column before a continuous one, then the column with the most admissible edges, then the one with the most entries, then the smallest index; every other column of the tree is substituted into it.
assumptions.alternatives: The binary of the row as the root always.
assumptions.measured: not measured as an alternative. 240 local dumps: alias depth 1 on highschool1-aigio, neos-1445765 and brazil3 (the binary is the root), 2 on bab2, bab6 and academictimetablesmall, 6 on the cryptanalysis instances; every scale is 1.

assumptions.title: Growth limit of the free singleton column (M1), which decides the instances behind m2_a
assumptions.statement: A free singleton column with a finite bound is substituted only when the growth factor of its pivot row stays within 1000.
assumptions.measured: 240 local dumps, this commit, with 1e300: nine instances smaller, none larger, 1.0005 / 1.0007 / 1.0007 against the default over the 237; the engine then equals or passes m2_a on every instance but traininstance2 (irish-electricity 412,803 / 71,555 / 43,092 against 414,574 / 71,742 / 43,156).

assumptions.title: What a doubleton equation spends (base code; repaired on the separate branch only)
assumptions.statement: On the branch to merge an edge spends the live entries of both its columns, once per edge. On the branch review-stage1c-m2-worth-2-doubleton a column is spent when it enters the batch.
assumptions.alternatives: Once per call, as built on the separate branch (a072b69c5).
assumptions.measured: One column in doubleton equations x[i] - p = 0: per edge, 5,000 equations end on max_rounds with 2,975 of 5,001 rows left; once per call, 200,000 are reduced to nothing in two calls. 240 local dumps, three settings: the same hash, sizes, rounds and flags either way; the doubleton work is lower on 51 instances (110,424,674 to 106,074,973 units in default mode) and six families make one call less on traininstance2 and traininstance6.

open: Owner's or merge's decision: take the doubleton repair (branch review-stage1c-m2-worth-2-doubleton, a072b69c54e2c402cc277e06a2acff30e4f18ce0, one commit on top of f0fc8b2cd) or not. It removes a real loss on star-shaped equalities (one column in thousands of doubleton equations, for instance copies of one variable) and one wasted call on traininstance2 and traininstance6, and it changes no reduced model on the 240 or the 17 local dumps; but an off run of that engine no longer equals the engine before the milestone in the work and calls of the Stage 1 families, so criterion 2 of the author's task then holds in hashes, sizes, rounds and flags only.

For the owner's test of the assumptions at the end: on the 240 and the 17 local dumps not one guard of simple probing refuses a row, so no run over solution quality on these sets can tell the alternatives apart (0/1 bounds, forcing tolerance, rounding guard, size of an offset, scale limit, balance, explicit bounds, one batch per call). They differ only on random models so far. Instances on which they bite would have to be found first.

The measurement switches exist only in my scratch build (/private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-acoerduek--claude-spares-spare-bsnTJo/c660eb6b-7edc-4afc-bf62-0442cb32d870/scratchpad/s1c_m2_worth/tools/instrument.py, build_inst.sh); if the owner wants any as an engine option it has to be built and covered by the checks.
No limit exists on substituting into long rows (bab2 and bab6: +11% and +10% time for 0.02% and 0.04% of the nonzeros). Whether to add one is a design decision; I built none.

The stored results of the author (gpu_presolve/results/bench240/s1c_m2_mac) are those of edd147a7e; after the repair the work of simple probing differs on highschool1-aigio and the two cryptanalysis instances. The results of the repaired engine are in gpu_presolve/results/bench240/s1c_m2_review_worth (default, primal, off).

Not done: nothing with a solver; nothing on the node or on the 44 testbed instances; solution quality for no assumption; no wrong engine through the check tool on the dumps; timing on a quiet machine (the sums here are good to about 0.3%, single small instances to a few percent).
